title: STALE BUILD on a machine NOT opted in to the folded bridge: a second Revit of the same year held the tools' DLLs; it clears itself
symptom: STALE BUILD in the ribbon/log on a machine that is NOT opted in to the folded bridge; loader.log shows "copy skipped for KOR.RevitTools.dll" / "Core.dll" and "cache NOT stamped current".
cause: The loader's cache is the folder Revit loads its assemblies from, so any assembly a running Revit of that year already holds cannot be replaced. Starting a second Revit of the same year makes its loader's sync fail on exactly those files. NOT the same as card 35: there the opted-in year's own instance locks the bridge DLL and the advice can never work; here the lock is transient.
check: C:\ProgramData\KOR\logs\loader.log for "copy skipped for KOR.RevitTools" with "NOT stamped current"; count running Revit.exe of that year.
fix: None needed: this is the loader's designed degradation, documented in KOR.RevitTools\docs\DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md as "a file is locked mid-sync (second Revit instance of the same year)". It clears itself: close ALL Revit windows of that year, then start one. The warning's advice is correct here.
plain: Explains that a 'Revit tools out of date' warning after opening a second Revit window is harmless and clears once all windows of that year are closed and one is reopened. Proof: KOR-306, 2026-10-27 14:41:50, two files skipped, one not-stamped event in 64 log lines (a second Revit 2026 started 10:29:29 held them); 6 of 6 earlier 2026 sync attempts since 10-13 succeeded (Revit Fleet, actions 11491/11497/11498). Also seen on KOR-305 2026, 23 Oct 16:45:13 (NetworkOps read 11494).
